findings.evidence: Independent source-extracted mocked call returned original start100 from _stat, then replaced the numeric PID with start999 before fake os.kill; the replacement received signal15. No real syscall or process was used. This outer function is AST-identical to v1.
findings.problem: The outer _signal_owned observes a matching PID/start then calls numeric os.kill. A tracked descendant may exit and be reaped by its still-running parent between those operations, letting the numeric PID identify an unrelated replacement at signal time. A PID/start precheck does not pin signal ownership.
findings.remediation: Use the existing owned_lifecycle_v2.signal_identity pidfd helper for each non-null original outer identity, require pidfd API availability before outer spawn, and preserve actual waits/adopted reaping/group absence gates.
findings.scope: Residual unchanged outer driver; inner v1 numeric process-group reuse defect is remediated in v2.
findings.title: Use pidfds for outer positive PID signals as well
